Latin word

cōnsentāneus

cōnsentāneus, cōnsentānea, cōnsentāneum

adjective; with cum or the dative, declension

agreeing with, in keeping with; logical, consistent (with something)

In this lexicon

  • consistent

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 3.6.2 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Phil. 9.15: mors ejus vītae sānctissimē āctae

  • logic

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.20: fōrmula Stōicōrum ratiōnī disciplīnaeque maximē cōnsentānea (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. logical (ratiōnī cōnsentāneus)

  • ratiōnī cōnsentāneus: reasonable

    classical

Examples

  • quod quidem erat cōnsentāneum cum iīs litterīs, quās ego Rōmae accēperam

    which was indeed consistent with the letter I had received at RomeCic. Fam. 3.6.2 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for consistent

  • ōrātiō verbīs discrepāns, sententiīs congruēns

    a speech differing in its words but consistent in its thoughtsCic. Leg. 1.30 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for consistent

  • Hoc nōn convenit cum eō quod heri dīxistī.

    This isn’t consistent with what you said yesterday.composed
